issues.issue: Does Financial Administration Act s.19 preclude collecting user fees in advance of the service?
issues.applicant_position: Section 19 allows fees only for services actually provided, so advance collection is unlawful.
issues.respondent_position: Section 19 does not prevent collecting service fees in advance of delivering a service.
issues.result_quote: There is nothing in section 19 which restricts the authority of the Governor in Council to adopt regulations requiring the payment of user fees prior

issues.issue: Are the sponsorship and visa applications one service, and is there a nexus between the fees and their cost?
issues.applicant_position: Two fees for one contingent service; no nexus when the visa service may be about 34 months away or never occur.
issues.respondent_position: Sponsorship and visa applications are effectively two parts of one service; the fees reflect practical efficiency.
issues.result_quote: a nexus or reasonable connection can be established between the fees collected for the permanent resident visa applications and the cost of processing these applications

issues.issue: Does the government holding the fees about 34 months before the service breach s.19 by profiting?
issues.applicant_position: Government profits from holding visa fees for about 34 months before any processing cost arises.
issues.result_quote: this, if established, would not offend section 19 of the Financial Administration Act.

issues.issue: Should the court compel different fee timing or notice because the timing is unreasonable?
issues.applicant_position: Government could easily amend the Regulations to notify applicants before collecting the visa fee.
issues.result_quote: In the absence of a legislative or constitutional constraint on the regulatory choices made by government, courts will not interfere to compel their own regulatory preferences
